title: Decomposition of the pairing into local terms
statement:
Let $(C,c,u)$, $(D,d,v)$ be an opposite pair of cohomological
correspondences as in [def-trf-supported-pairing], with intersection
support $E=E(C,D)$ (the fiber product of the two supports of
[def-trf-correspondence-between-pairs]) and Borel–Moore section
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_E\to\omega_{E,A}$. Suppose that
$E$ is a finite disjoint union

$$
E=\coprod_{\beta\in B}\beta
$$

of open-and-closed subschemes $j_\beta:\beta\hookrightarrow E$, each
proper over $s$. For $\beta\in B$ let
$\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}|_\beta:=j_\beta^*\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}:A_\beta\to\omega_{\beta,A}$
be the restricted pairing and

$$
\LT_\beta(u,v)=\int_\beta\bigl(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}|_\beta\bigr)\in A
$$

the local term of the pair on $\beta$, both as in
[def-trf-local-term-pair]; the restricted pairing is the restriction
of [lem-trf-integration-component-sum] (both are the composite
$A_\beta\simeq Lj_\beta^*A_E\to Lj_\beta^*\omega_{E,A}\cong\omega_{\beta,A}$),
and for $v=1_K$ and $\beta\subseteq\Fix(c)$ the local term is
$\LT_\beta(u)$ of [def-trf-local-term]. Then $E$ is proper over $s$ and

$$
\int_E\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}
=\sum_{\beta\in B}\LT_\beta(u,v).
$$

If $E=\emptyset$ both sides are $0$. Moreover, for a perfect
$A$-complex $P$ on $s$ and an endomorphism $w:P\to P$, regarded as an
endocorrespondence with support $s$ (whose sole component is $s$),

$$
\LT_s(w)=\LT_s(w,1_P)=\tr_A(w\mid P).
$$

proof.text:
The opposite-pair conventions of [def-trf-supported-pairing] in the statement make $E$ separated of finite type over $s$, with the finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ and a defined section $A_E\to\omega_{E,A}$. Thus the separated-finite-type and coefficient hypotheses of [lem-trf-integration-component-sum] hold. The dualizing complexes and integrals are those of the current [def-trf-integration]: the exceptional functor and counit are restricted to the full constructible finite-Tor categories, and the proper comparison is applied to their bounded etale-origin inputs. The admissibility conventions of the supported-pairing and local-term definitions supply these domains; no ambient exceptional adjoint is required. Apply [lem-trf-integration-component-sum] to $T=E$, the finite
decomposition $E=\coprod_{\beta\in B}\beta$ and
$\tau=\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$: it shows that $E$ is proper
over $s$, so that $\int_E$ of [def-trf-integration] is defined, and
that

$$
\int_E\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}
=\sum_{\beta\in B}\int_\beta\bigl(\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}|_\beta\bigr)
=\sum_{\beta\in B}\LT_\beta(u,v),
$$

the last equality being the definition of the local terms in
[def-trf-local-term-pair]; if $E=\emptyset$, apply the lemma first with its empty-index decomposition to obtain $\int_E\langle u,v\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=0$. Every displayed piece $\beta$ is then empty; applying the same empty-index case to each $\beta$ gives $\LT_\beta(u,v)=0$, so the displayed sum is also zero even when $B$ is nonempty. In the diagonal specialization take $(Y,L)=(X,K)$ and $(D,d,v)=(X,\Delta_X,1_K)$, so that
$\langle u,1_K\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}=\Tr_c(u)$ by
[lem-trf-trace-class-diagonal-pairing], the restriction to a component
$\beta\subseteq\Fix(c)$ is the composite used in [def-trf-local-term],
whence $\LT_\beta(u,1_K)=\LT_\beta(u)$, as also recorded in
[def-trf-local-term-pair].

For the point case, $E=s$, $B=\{s\}$, and $j_s$ and the structure map $a_s$ are identities. By [def-trf-dualizing-complex], $\omega_{s,A}=R\operatorname{id}_s^!A_s$, canonically identified with $A_s$ by the identity-morphism adjunction comparison; restriction to the sole component is the section itself. Use precisely the proper comparison $P_a:Ra_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!$ and the constructible counit $\varepsilon_a(A_s)$ in the current [def-trf-integration]. Here $Ra_*$ and $La^*$ have their canonical identity identifications. Write $\lambda:A_s\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra^!A_s$ for the corresponding exceptional identity comparison, so that $\varepsilon_a(A_s)\circ Ra_!\lambda\circ P_a(A_s)=1_{A_s}$; this is the identity-adjunction counit equation, with the proper comparison included. For a section $\tau=\lambda\circ t$, naturality of $P_a$ gives
$$
\varepsilon_a(A_s)\circ Ra_!\tau\circ P_a(A_s)
=\varepsilon_a(A_s)\circ Ra_!\lambda\circ P_a(A_s)\circ t=t.
$$
The ordinary unit is the identity in these coordinates. Thus the derived composite defining $\int_s\tau$ is $R\Gamma(s,t):A[0]\to A[0]$, and the scalar prescribed by [def-trf-integration] is $H^0(R\Gamma(s,t))(1)$. In particular this integral is the usual scalar of the section under the canonical identity comparisons, without requiring chosen compactification candidates to be literally equal. Apply this to $\tau=\langle w,1_P\rangle_{\mathrm{LV}}$. The point normalization [prop-trf-pairing-point-normalization], with $Q=P$, $u=w$, $v=1_P$, identifies its scalar with $\tr_A(1_P\circ w\mid P)=\tr_A(w\mid P)$. The definitions [def-trf-local-term] and [def-trf-local-term-pair] identify $\LT_s(w,1_P)$ with this integral. Finally the diagonal specialization proved in step 1, for $X=s$, $K=P$, $u=w$, gives $\LT_s(w)=\LT_s(w,1_P)$.
